usecase.comment: Detection.md entry 39 and exact lower-case `usecase-beta` ... followed by common whitespace or end of text. Header/body statements must be on separate physical lines. Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit are trivia. Follows usecase.md#detection.

patterns.comment: Read a native percent comment after ASCII padding at a line, header or directive boundary. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.
A bare percent pair or nondirective percent-brace line after the header is a native comment through before LF. Follows usecase.md#whitespace-comments-and-directives-in-every-context.
Read the json keyword and id before its at-sign data block. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and usecase.md#json-context.
Read the JSON at sign and balanced object in one data scope. Follows usecase.md#json-context.
patterns.name: meta.data.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read style targets or style class names, followed by property names and complete property values. Follows usecase.md#grammar.
Read a CSS property word, hyphenated identifier, or markerless prefix and word. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and usecase.md#categories-and-unquoted-text.
Read one whole style property value, leaving trailing whitespace outside its scope. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and usecase.md#grammar.
Read an escaped comma inside the one property value. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

patterns.name: punctuation.separator.comma.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read the separator between style declarations. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Note-statement is note, for, id and node-label through line-end; Word keywords and booleans inside the label are text. Directives can stand between complete components. A separator-led comment ends the value. Follows usecase.md#rejections-outside-the-grammar.

A split-association has a markerless, backward, circle or cross opener, edge-label text, then the closing relationship operator. Word keywords and booleans in the label are text; complete arrows remain indivisible. Follows usecase.md#grammar.

Rule 10: Keyword order is `usecase-beta`, `actor`, `systemBoundary`, `end`, `direction`, `TD`, `TB`, `BT`, `LR`, `RL`, `note`, `for`, `json`, `classDef`, `class`, `style`, `include`, `extend`, `true`, `false`. Only include/extend are case-insensitive. A longer Identifier wins over a keyword. The style declaration rule above owns classDef and style, so their spelling is not repeated here. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

patterns.name: constant.language.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read a listed layout direction. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read the semantic dependency relation. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Rule 13: stereotype-open: <<; enter stereotype context. take all characters through immediately before the first `>>`, provided that text contains no physical line break and is not all common whitespace. Stereotype interiors are text; a closer inside a directive does not end the unit. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Stereotype text runs through before the first double angle closer. A separator-led comment ends the current value run while the stereotype context remains open. Follows usecase.md#stereotype-context and common.md#comment-lines.

Rules 11, 12 and 15 to 21: generalization `--|>`, dependency-arrow `..>`, forward-solid (two or more dashes followed by >), backward-solid (< followed by two or more dashes), forward-circle `--o`, backward-circle `o--`, forward-cross `--x`, backward-cross `x--`, markerless-solid (two or more dashes). Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.arrow.mermaid

patterns.comment: Rule 14: class-separator: `:::`. class-suffix = ":::" id ( "," id )*. ASCII space/tab may stand between the units. Directives may separate the class marker, complete class names and commas. Follows usecase.md#grammar.

Rules 25 and 26: brackets [, then ]; parentheses (, then ). actor-name = id ( "(" node-label ")" )? ...; entity-name = ( id ( "(" node-label ")" | "[" node-label "]" )? ... ). The label inside is colored as a string. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
Rule 28: hash-color: # and a positive run of ASCII hexadecimal digits. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
patterns.name: support.constant.property-value.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read a complete same-line tag without a scope of its own, preserving the surrounding text scope. Quoted attribute values do not close the surrounding double-quoted string. Read directives whole; one containing the first greater-than sign ends the tag after that directive. Stop before an ordinary double quote or separator-led common comment for the enclosing context to read. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes, common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary, and common.md#comment-lines.
Rules 2 and 29: A string reads through its matching delimiter without escapes; markdown strings end at a backtick followed by a double quote. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Rule 32: The number rule reads digits with an optional decimal fraction having digits on both sides, or a leading dot and digits; it can then take ASCII letters as a unit suffix. The Identifier rule is earlier, so `1mg` is an id while `1.5px` is a number unit. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

patterns.comment: Rule 31: identifier: Maximal positive ASCII word run. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
patterns.name: variable.mermaid

patterns.comment: Rules 23, 24 and 27: at `@`; braces {, then }; comma, colon. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

usecase-object.comment: Balance nested JSON braces and quotes inside opaque text without adding delimiter or string scopes. Follows usecase.md#json-context.

usecase-json-html-tag.comment: Read quoted HTML attribute values as part of the surrounding text. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes.

usecase-boolean.comment: Rule 10: true and false are keywords, with Identifier as their longer alternative. metadata-property = ( id | plain-string ) ":" ( id | plain-string | "true" | "false" ). Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

usecase-class-names.comment: A class list consists of whole ids separated by commas; Directives may lie between its complete names and punctuation. Follows usecase.md#grammar.

patterns.comment: Each class in class-suffix is an id, with ASCII space/tab permitted between units. Follows usecase.md#grammar.
patterns.name: variable.mermaid

patterns.comment: Class-suffix = ":::" id ( "," id )*, with ASCII space/tab allowed between units. Follows usecase.md#grammar.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.comma.mermaid

usecase-metadata.comment: Metadata is contiguous @{, optional properties separated by commas or newlines, and a closing brace. A property has an exact id or plain-string key, colon, and id, plain-string or boolean value. Follows usecase.md#grammar and usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
usecase-metadata.name: meta.data.mermaid

patterns.comment: Read the unquoted actor and boundary types and edge animation values listed in the native metadata table as fixed values. Quoted values keep their string scopes. Follows usecase.md#rejections-outside-the-grammar.
An unquoted metadata key is an exact id followed by a colon. Directives may stand in the whitespace between the whole id and colon. Follows usecase.md#grammar.

patterns.name: punctuation.separator.comma.mermaid
patterns.comment: Metadata properties are separated by commas. Follows usecase.md#grammar.
Metadata-property is an id or plain-string key, a colon, then an id, plain-string, true or false value; quoted keys precede the colon. Follows usecase.md#grammar.
patterns.name: punctuation.separator.key-value.mermaid
string.unquoted.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read a bare native metadata text value. Follows usecase.md#rejections-outside-the-grammar.

usecase-accessibility.comment: Rules 6 to 8: Accessibility forms start at an ASCII-HWS-only physical-line start. Colon values take the remainder of the physical line, including inline percent pairs. The block closes at its first brace. A separator-led common comment ends the surrounding value. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and common.md#comment-lines.

patterns.comment: Read an accessibility description block at a line, header or directive boundary after ASCII padding. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.
Rule 6: Description text ends at the first closing brace. A comment region is trivia inside the block and ends the current value run. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Read an accessibility keyword and colon with its physical-line value at a line, header or directive boundary. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary.

usecase-plain-string.comment: Rule 29: Plain strings have matching quotes without escapes and no physical LF in the text read by the lexer. A common region can remove an authored LF; keep the enclosing quote context while value runs stop before separator-led comments. An unclosed or otherwise rejected string may stay open under the common grammar limits. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and common.md#comment-lines.

patterns.comment: Rule 29: The matching quote ends this plain string; common comment regions do not supply a closing quote. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Rule 29: Read plain-string content without quote escapes. End this value run before a separator-led common comment and resume within the quote context. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
Read quoted HTML attribute values as part of the surrounding text. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes.
Rule 29: The matching quote ends this plain string; common comment regions do not supply a closing quote. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

Rule 29: Read plain-string content without quote escapes. End this value run before a separator-led common comment and resume within the quote context. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

usecase-label.comment: Word keywords and booleans in node-label and edge-label are text. Strings are separate alternatives; an HTML attribute quote is changed before it can start a string. Follows usecase.md#categories-and-unquoted-text.

patterns.comment: An unquoted label needs at least one LabelText unit and keeps interior spaces; strings are separate alternatives. Tags inside label text own their attribute quotes; an unrelated quote ends the text context. End before a separator-led common comment. In an edge label, relationship operators end the text. Follows usecase.md#categories-and-unquoted-text and common.md#comment-lines.

Read each Identifier, CSS identifier or decimal number whole before trying the next arrow boundary, so an o or x inside it stays label text. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules and usecase.md#categories-and-unquoted-text.

usecase-html-tag.comment: Only attribute quotes change; label delimiters and relationship operators still end label text, including inside a quoted attribute. Shape delimiters and operators are not LabelText; an unrelated quote starts a string. Follows usecase.md#categories-and-unquoted-text and common.md#html-attribute-quotes.

patterns.comment: Equals and a paired double quote open an attribute value. Label delimiters and relationship operators still end the surrounding text. Follows usecase.md#categories-and-unquoted-text and common.md#html-attribute-quotes.

usecase-style-string.comment: Keep a complete plain-string component, including its commas and quotes, inside one style property value. Follows usecase.md#grammar and usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

patterns.comment: Read a double-quoted CSS value component without changing its property-value scope. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
Read a single-quoted CSS value component without changing its property-value scope. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.

usecase-metadata-property-name.comment: Read a native metadata key as a string or an unquoted property name. Follows usecase.md#grammar.

patterns.comment: Read a bare Identifier key. Follows usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules.
patterns.name: support.type.property-name.mermaid

usecase-json-quote.comment: Protect JSON braces inside double quotes while retaining the surrounding text scope. Follows usecase.md#json-context.

patterns.comment: Keep JSON quoted contents, HTML attribute quotes and escaped characters in opaque text. Follows usecase.md#json-context and common.md#html-attribute-quotes.
Read quoted HTML attribute values as part of the surrounding text. Follows common.md#html-attribute-quotes.
Protect the next JSON character without changing its text scope, preserving directives. Follows usecase.md#json-context.
